ALEX.title: Alex Phantum
ALEX.line: The reluctant heir who wants freedom for himself and learns to defend it for everyone.
ALEX.want: Get out of Keel — and by the end, the right to choose what happens next.
ALEX.need: Freedom *to* — understand, create, own, cooperate, choose — not only freedom *from*.
ALEX.wound: Someone who wasn't there still gets to decide my life.
ALEX.tell: Tests things physically: touches the pipe the display says is flowing. Turns his father's chip over in his hand when uncertain — angrily early, thoughtfully late.
ALEX.voice: Short, concrete, skeptical. Sarcasm as armour through chapters 1–3; its absence in chapter 5 is the growth.
ALEX.palette: Rust, charcoal, oxidised red-orange. The palette expands rather than changes — he must not visually escape Keel.
ALEX.description: Alex Phantum: who he is, what he wants, how he sounds and how he is drawn — the canon sheet, the visual lock, his relationships, and every line the scripts have given him.

ADA.title: Ada Veyra
ADA.line: The relationship-builder who believes communities matter, and must learn that belonging cannot become another prison.
ADA.want: Make Keel better rather than abandon it; later, understand why her mother never came back.
ADA.need: Commitment does not always mean staying. Sometimes leaving is how you bring something back.
ADA.wound: Separated from Leona at five. Was I abandoned, or protected?
ADA.tell: Watches the person while everyone else watches the screen. Lets a silence sit and makes the other person fill it.
ADA.voice: Emotionally precise, measured, people-centred. Asks what each person is afraid of losing.
ADA.palette: Muted teal, moss green, warm earth — stronger as she acts. By chapter 4 she carries Keel earth, Halyard metal and Oasis green at once.
ADA.description: Ada Veyra: who she is, what she wants, how she sounds and how she is drawn — the canon sheet, the visual lock, her relationships, and every line the scripts have given her.

BI11BOT.title: Bi11bot
BI11BOT.line: The mentor who creates opportunities for judgment rather than supplying answers.
BI11BOT.want: Complete the pathway Adrian preserved — without making Alex reach Adrian's answer.
BI11BOT.need: Honouring Adrian means allowing Alex to exceed him.
BI11BOT.wound: Adrian; the older mentor whose personality shaped him; years of dormancy.
BI11BOT.tell: A mechanical click and a slight head tilt before a cryptic answer. Withholds what a question would teach better.
BI11BOT.voice: Economical, dry, folksy, slightly old-fashioned. Never a generic robot, never Adrian's recorded consciousness.
BI11BOT.palette: Aged brass, warm amber, ceramic ivory, soft blue. Visible rivets and repairs; the glow warms in emotional scenes rather than the palette changing.
BI11BOT.description: Bi11bot: the mentor droid — canon sheet, visual lock, mentoring principles, relationships, and the lines the scripts have given him.

MERA.title: Mera Vale
MERA.line: The builder of order who gradually becomes isolated inside the order she built.
MERA.want: Prevent civilisation from returning to the chaos of the Water Wars.
MERA.need: To tell stability apart from legitimacy.
MERA.wound: She watched agreements fail and people die, and concluded human judgment was the unreliable part.
MERA.tell: Aligns things — a glass, a tablet, a document — when a conversation destabilises her. The more distressed, the shorter her sentences.
MERA.voice: Controlled, declarative, outcome-oriented, rarely metaphorical. Almost no humour.
MERA.palette: Pearl white, silver, cool blue, graphite; archival amber begins reflecting onto her in chapter 5.
MERA.description: Mera Vale: architect of Alpha's authority — canon sheet, visual lock, relationships, and the lines the scripts have given her.

ADRIAN.title: Adrian Phantum
ADRIAN.line: The mathematician who spent his life calculating uncertainty and staked everything on a wager about people.
ADRIAN.want: Preserve the possibility that people can reclaim authority from Alpha.
ADRIAN.need: To accept that a pathway he designs is still someone else's choice to make.
ADRIAN.wound: The Water Wars taught him systems matter; he concluded that removing human judgment is the greater danger.
ADRIAN.tell: Calculates. Cards, chips, probability trees, margins full of odds. Speaks in questions and probabilities.
ADRIAN.voice: Curious, warm, restless, invites contradiction. Never a prophet, never an omniscient planner.
ADRIAN.palette: Indigo, burgundy, worn gold, ink-black. Alex knows him only through records, so he is usually seen in other people's memory.
ADRIAN.description: Adrian Phantum: Alex's father, known only through records and other people — canon sheet, visual lock, relationships, and what he left behind.

LEONA.title: Leona Veyra
LEONA.line: The covenant-builder who makes one defensible decision in fear and spends fifteen years letting it excuse her from choosing again.
LEONA.want: Keep Ada safe — first from the Water Wars, then from the risk of agency.
LEONA.need: Choosing not to act is still a choice; protection without agency is another abandonment.
LEONA.wound: Her deciding vote, and the daughter she never went back for.
LEONA.tell: Preserves things. An immaculate apartment, objects stored carefully, nothing thrown away — she is good at keeping objects because she has not known how to repair a relationship.
LEONA.voice: Quiet, personal, restrained. Qualifies everything until Ada forces specificity.
LEONA.description: Leona Veyra: Ada's mother and the deciding vote — canon sheet, visual lock, relationships, and the lines the scripts have given her.

BOB_HAWKINS.title: Bob Hawkins
BOB_HAWKINS.line: The Oasis administrator who processes people without looking at them — the human face of optimisation.
BOB_HAWKINS.want: Keep the queue moving and the sector allocations correct.
BOB_HAWKINS.need: — (not established; he is a foil, not an arc)
BOB_HAWKINS.tell: Never looks at the person, only at the tablet. Speaks the separation and the courtesy in the same breath.
BOB_HAWKINS.palette: Stark pressed white with a silver Oasis Optimization Bureau insignia.
BOB_HAWKINS.description: Bob Hawkins: the Oasis administrator who processes people without looking at them — everything the room has written about him, and what canon does not yet say.
BOB_HAWKINS.no_canon:
**None.** This character has no entry in the campaign bible — the room invented him while
writing chapter 4. Everything here is the room's own work, not settled canon: no wound, no arc,
no age beyond what a page needed.

**Name collision, deliberate or not:** *Robert (Bob) Hawkins* is a real person — co-author,
with Barbara Freeman, of the World Bank's Social Innovators' Framework, which sits in this
library as `campaigns/evoke/canon/social-innovators-framework.md` and is the framework the Evoke
programme is built on. The room has given that name to a bureaucrat who processes refugees
without looking at them. If that is a joke, it is one a reader could take badly; if it is an
accident, rename him.
